title: Tenali Raman Tale 129

full_text:
For the grand festival of Vijaya Dashami, King Krishnadevaraya commissioned a magnificent Navaratna (Nine Gems) royal diadem from the guild of imperial jewelers.
When the crown was delivered, it was a dazzling spectacle: diamonds, rubies, emeralds, sapphires, pearls, corals, topaz, cat’s eyes, and garnets blazed in golden filigree.
The Chief Goldsmith swore: 'Every gem is of first-water purity, tested by fire and stone!'

However, an anonymous note reached Tenali Raman, warning that the central ruby—a stone valued at ten thousand gold coins—was an imitation made of red Bohemian crystal foil!

Tenali examined the crown in the presence of the King and the jewelers.
To the naked eye, the red gem sparkled with intense fire.
The jewelers scoffed: 'Tenali is a poet; what does he know of lapidary arts?'

Tenali asked for a common unglazed terracotta brick and a bowl of fresh lemon juice.
Tenali explained:
'A genuine Burmese ruby possesses a hardness of nine on the mineral scale; it cannot be scratched by hardened steel, nor does natural sunlight alter its inner refraction when immersed in acid.
Foil-backed crystal, on the other hand, relies upon a thin layer of silver-mercury amalgam painted on its rear facets to reflect light.'

Tenali placed the central red gem gently into the warm lemon juice.
He then took an unglazed terracotta tile and rubbed the surface of the gem firmly against the rough clay.
Within thirty seconds, a fine grey powder began to rub off the stone, and the bright crimson fire inside the gem suddenly dissolved into a dull, pale, scratched piece of common red glass!
The acid had dissolved the false silver foil backing, exposing the cheap crystal underneath!

The Chief Goldsmith turned white as chalk, falling to his knees on the marble floor:
'Mercy, Maharaj! I substituted the real ruby and hid it in my workshop safe!'

The real Burmese ruby was recovered, the dishonest jeweler was dismissed and fined, and King Krishnadevaraya embraced Tenali Raman:
'Tenali, thy simple lemon juice and clay brick have defended the honor of the imperial crown!'
Tenali smiled, reminding the court that genuine truth fears no friction, while false brilliance dissolves under testing.
moral: Flawless integrity shines without fear; true gems need no painted foils to prove their brilliance.
